Note::TexAccessor::tables¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::tables() const

Extract Complete table/table* Environments¶

tables() extracts every complete \begin{table}...\end{table} and \begin{table*}...\end{table*} region, including its delimiters, as one token per match, in source order. It is useful when a document’s floating tables must be collected, counted, or analyzed independently of the surrounding prose.

Both the starred and unstarred forms are recognized in the same pass and interleaved in document order — this is a genuine superset of what a single generic env("table") call returns, which only matches one exact environment name at a time. A table environment nested inside another table environment is captured as one token spanning from the outer \begin{table} to its matching outer \end{table}; the inner \begin{table}...\end{table} is not separately extracted, since matching is non-overlapping and outer-first. An escaped \\begin{table} is not a real environment opener and produces no match, and an unterminated \begin{table}broken with no closing tag is dropped rather than partially returned.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted region — delimiters included — in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells, malformed markers, and cells without a table environment produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted.

Example 1: Starred, Unstarred, Nested, Escaped, And Broken Forms¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\begin{table*}star\end{table*} x \begin{table}plain\end{table})",
    R"(\begin{table}outer \begin{table}inner\end{table} tail\end{table})",
    R"(\\begin{table}escaped\\end{table} \begin{table}broken)"});
const auto tables = source.tex().tables();

std::cout << tables.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{table*}star\\end{table*}", "\\begin{table}plain\\end{table}", "\\begin{table}outer \\begin{table}inner\\end{table} tail\\end{table}"]

Cell 0 contributes both the starred and unstarred region as separate tokens, in document order. Cell 1’s nested tables collapse into the single outer-spanning token. Cell 2 contributes nothing: the escaped pair and the unterminated \begin{table}broken both fail to match.

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = tables.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Cell 0 owns two tokens, cell 1 owns the one outer-spanning token, and cell 2 owns none.

Example 3: A 2-D Grid, Ragged Ownership Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\begin{table}A\end{table})", "plain",
                             R"(\begin{table*}B\end{table*})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto grid_batch = grid.tex().tables();
std::cout << grid_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{table}A\\end{table}", "\\begin{table*}B\\end{table*}"]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().tables().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().tables();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "tables Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
tables Int64: rejected
